title: AI Behind India's 'Mahabharat' Heads to Indonesia to Bring Nusantara Myths to the Screen
excerpt: Galleri5 and Collective Studios' Historyverse will work with Indonesian creators and the Singhasari Special Economic Zone on mythology, fantasy and history projects, starting with 'Echoes of Nusantara'
body:
• The AI technology behind the Hindi-language series 'Mahabharat: Ek Dharmayudh' on Star Plus and JioHotstar is expanding to Indonesia through Galleri5 and Collective Studios' Historyverse.
  • Historyverse is partnering with Galleri5 and the Singhasari Special Economic Zone to develop film and series projects from Indonesian myths and history.
  • The first project under discussion is 'Echoes of Nusantara,' an original mythology-adventure, with Indonesian creatives and cultural specialists working alongside Historyverse's team.
  • Executives frame the pact as proof that the next global franchises will not all come from Hollywood, and that Indian-built production tools can help local stories travel.

The technology that put an AI-made Mahabharat on Indian prime-time television is about to retell a different archipelago's myths. Galleri5, the AI studio within Collective Artists Network, and Collective Studios' Historyverse plan to create film and series properties drawn from Indonesia's myths and history, according to Variety's report syndicated by Europe Says.

Historyverse, which handles original IP and studio work for Collective Artists Network, is partnering with Galleri5 and the Singhasari Special Economic Zone on the venture. The slate will span mythology, fantasy, history and animation, with Indonesian creatives and cultural specialists working alongside Historyverse's IP development team using production tools Galleri5 built in India.

From Kurukshetra to Nusantara

The first project being discussed is “Echoes of Nusantara,” a working title for an original mythology-adventure. Historyverse will run creative development, production and IP packaging, and will collaborate with local talent to get projects ready for possible financing, production and distribution outside Indonesia, the report said.

The template is 'Mahabharat: Ek Dharmayudh,' the Hindi-language series launched by JioStar and Collective Media Network for Star Plus and streaming on JioHotstar. Galleri5 built and ran the AI filmmaking technology behind the show, a credit it has used to argue that AI-native storytelling can sustain mainstream television.

“The next global entertainment franchises will not all come from Hollywood,” said Vijay Subramaniam, founder and group CEO of Collective Artists Network. “Every market has stories that deserve to travel further, and Indonesia has an extraordinary wealth of them. Our ambition with Collective Studios' Historyverse is to work with Indonesian creators to develop these stories into films, series and larger entertainment properties for the world.”

What Galleri5 is bringing

Galleri5's main product, G5 AI Studio, brings together more than 200 AI models with purpose-built tools for storyboarding, designing characters and worlds, animation, VFX and film-quality video. More than 10,000 ads and videos have been made on the platform, according to the companies.

The studio is now developing workflows for Historyverse's theatrical slate, which includes 'Chiranjeevi Hanuman – The Eternal' and 'Krishna.' As MediaBrief reported from the company's NXTinAI showcase in Hyderabad, Galleri5 is also developing 'Chiranjeevi Hanuman' as a full-length AI feature with Star Studio18 for theatrical release, and a teaser has already screened in cinemas.

“The next generation of global cinema will be built on a very different technology foundation,” said Rahul Regulapati, founder and CEO of Galleri5 and a partner at Collective Artists Network. “We've already demonstrated what this technology can do through films and television in India. Now, together with Indonesia's extraordinary creative talent and Collective's studio capabilities, we have an opportunity to take locally rooted stories to audiences around the world.”

Why Indonesia, and why now

For Indonesian partners, the deal is framed as industrial policy as much as entertainment. Airlangga Hartarto, Indonesia's coordinating minister for economic affairs and chairman of the National Council for Special Economic Zones, said the country had no plans to sit on the sidelines of AI development or simply act as a consumer of the technology. “We intend to help shape it,” he said, arguing that special economic zones can turn that ambition into productivity, skilled jobs and growth.

Singhasari will introduce the venture to Indonesian creators, studios, investors, distributors and creative-economy institutions, and help set up local partnerships and routes to market. KRAT David Santoso KR, CEO of Lokanima and Singhasari Special Economic Zone, noted that the Kingdom of Singhasari flourished eight centuries ago on the land the zone now occupies, enriched by hundreds of years of contact with India. “Today, with our partners from India, we are bringing that history back to life, this time by mastering the AI transformation,” he said.

India's ambassador to Indonesia, Sandeep Chakravorty, made the cultural link explicit: the Ramayana and the Mahabharata have been part of Indonesian temple culture, wayang puppet theatre and the popular imagination for over a millennium. “Today, India and Indonesia are writing the next chapter of that shared story with artificial intelligence,” he said. For diaspora viewers who grew up watching the Mahabharat at home and know those epics in Balinese and Javanese forms too, the pact lands on familiar ground — an Indian-built tool, now making room for Indonesia's own legends to travel in return.
